auth_back_to_sign_in: A link under the forgot-password form, after "Remembered your password?": back to the sign-in page.
auth_change_email_bad_link: The link from the email that confirms a new address is missing a part: it can't be used.
auth_change_email_busy: Beside a spinner while the link from the email that confirms a new address is checked.
auth_change_email_done_title: Heading: the account's email address is now the new one.
auth_change_email_failed_title: Heading over what went wrong when changing the account's email address.
auth_confirm_password_label: [short] A field's label: the password typed a second time, to check it. Confirm is an adjective here (the confirmation of the password), not a button.
auth_display_name_label: [short] Sign-up field's label: the name shown to others, which may stay empty. The username is a separate field.
auth_display_name_placeholder: [short] Grey example text inside the empty display-name field on sign-up, in a half-width column. Lowercase on purpose.
auth_email_label: [short] A field's label: the account's email address.
auth_email_placeholder: Grey example inside the empty email field on sign-in, sign-up and the forgot-password page. Keep it a well-formed address at example.com (a domain reserved for examples); the part before @ may use your language's word, e.g. du@example.com.
auth_forgot_busy: [short] The forgot-password page's button while its request is being sent.
auth_forgot_link: [short] A link beside the password field's label on sign-in: opens the page that sends a reset email.
auth_forgot_remembered: Under the forgot-password form, followed by the link "Back to sign in".
auth_forgot_sent: Shown after a reset email is asked for. It never says whether the account exists, on purpose.
auth_forgot_title: Heading of the page that sends a password reset email.
auth_go_to_duvet: [short] A button after an email link worked: opens the app. Duvet is the app's name.
auth_go_to_sign_in: [short] A button that opens the sign-in page.
auth_new_password_label: [short] A field's label on the reset-password page: the password the account will have.
auth_password_hide: Name of the eye button at the end of a password field while the password is shown: a press hides it again.
auth_password_label: [short] A field's label on sign-in: the account's password.
auth_password_show: Name of the eye button at the end of a password field: a press shows what was typed.
auth_passwords_differ: Under the second password field when the two passwords typed aren't the same.
auth_reset_busy: Beside a spinner while the new password is saved.
auth_reset_confirm_placeholder: Grey hint inside the empty second password field on the reset-password page.
auth_reset_done_title: Heading: the password was reset (a past participle, not a button).
auth_reset_failed_title: Heading over what went wrong when resetting the password.
auth_reset_no_token: The reset link opened has no code in it, so the password can't be reset. A token is the code in the link.
auth_reset_password_placeholder: Grey hint inside the empty new-password field. # is the shortest length a password may have (8).
auth_reset_remove_devices: A checkbox on the page where the person picks a new password: every device of theirs comes off their account with it.
auth_reset_remove_devices_note: Under auth_reset_remove_devices: when to use it, and what it costs (a recovery key to set a device up again).
auth_session_not_renewed: An error a request in a second window (Settings, a Space's settings) can show: the app's main window keeps the sign-in fresh, and it didn't in time. Nobody is signed out.
auth_sign_in: [short] A button or link: sign in to an account (a verb).
auth_sign_in_busy: [short] The sign-in button while it's being sent.
auth_sign_in_create_account: A link under the sign-in form, after "New to Duvet?": opens sign-up.
auth_sign_in_lead: Under the sign-in page's heading. Duvet is the app's name.
auth_sign_in_missing_both: Shown when sign-in is pressed with both fields empty.
auth_sign_in_missing_email: Shown when sign-in is pressed without an email address.
auth_sign_in_missing_password: Shown when sign-in is pressed without a password.
auth_sign_in_new: Under the sign-in form, followed by the link "Create an account". Duvet is the app's name.
auth_sign_in_password_placeholder: Grey hint inside the empty password field on sign-in.
auth_sign_up_busy: [short] The sign-up button while the account is being made.
auth_sign_up_confirm_placeholder: [short] Grey hint inside the empty second password field on sign-up, in a half-width column: type the same password again. Lowercase on purpose.
auth_sign_up_have_account: Under the sign-up form, followed by the link "Sign in".
auth_sign_up_lead: Under the sign-up page's heading. It goes on from the tagline "a cozy place to talk" (Duvet's), so it starts in lowercase.
auth_sign_up_password_label: [short] Sign-up field's label, in a half-width column. # is the shortest length a password may have (8).
auth_sign_up_password_placeholder: [short] Grey hint inside the empty password field on sign-up: a password of # characters or more. # is the shortest length (8).
auth_tagline: Duvet's tagline, under its name beside the sign-in pages. Lowercase on purpose.
auth_terms_agree: Beside the checkbox on sign-up. <terms>…</terms> is a link that opens the terms: keep the tags around the words that name them.
auth_terms_title: Heading of the sheet that shows the terms of use.
auth_username_hint: Under the username field on sign-up: the characters a username may have (letters, digits, dots and underscores) and its length, 2 to 32. People mention someone with @username.
auth_username_label: [short] Sign-up field's label, in a half-width column beside the display name: the unique name people mention with @username. Not the display name.
auth_username_placeholder: [short] Grey example text inside the empty username field on sign-up, in a half-width column. Lowercase on purpose.
auth_verify_busy: Beside a spinner while the link from the email that confirms the account's address is checked.
auth_verify_done_title: Heading: the account's email address is confirmed.
auth_verify_failed_title: Heading over what went wrong when confirming the account's email address.
auth_verify_no_token: The confirmation link opened has no code in it. A token is the code in the link.
e2e_already_member: In the add-members sheet of an encrypted group, when the person picked someone who is a member already.
e2e_approval_ask: The title of a question on a device of the person's, when a new device asks to read their encrypted conversations.
e2e_approval_asks: Under e2e_approval_ask, on a device of the person's that may approve the new one.
e2e_approval_close: [short] Closes the approval's dialog once it ended (a verb).
e2e_approval_code: Above the six digits the approving device shows.
e2e_approval_code_hint: Under the code's field on the new device: where the six digits come from, the screen of the person's other device that approves it (a computer or a phone).
e2e_approval_confirm: [short] Approves the new device, once it accepted the code (a verb).
e2e_approval_confirm_after: Under the six digits: confirm only once the new device said it accepted them.
e2e_approval_failed: When approving a new device failed for a reason that passes.
e2e_approval_fingerprint_line: Under e2e_code_fingerprint on the device that approves, on the web and in the desktop app, whose own box (src/bun/e2e/confirm.ts, COMPARE_WITH_THE_BOX) says the same words. The Duvet app on a computer shows the new device's fingerprint in a box of its own, outside its window; Duvet in a browser shows it on its page.
e2e_approval_listed: In the approval's dialog, when the device asking is already on the person's device list.
e2e_approval_name: On a line of its own under e2e_approval_fingerprint_line, on the device that approves. {name} is the name the new device gives itself, such as Chrome on Linux, which whoever sent its request writes: it's quoted as that device's own word, never part of what the person compares or types.
e2e_approval_no: [short] Answers e2e_approval_ask: the new device isn't the person's, and its request goes.
e2e_approval_over: When an approval took longer than its ten minutes, or another one took its place.
e2e_approval_over_here: In the approval's dialog, when its attempt ended (ten minutes passed, or the new device began another).
e2e_approval_title: The title of the approval's question once the person said the device is theirs.
e2e_approval_unfinished: Under e2e_approval_asks, when this device approved the new one before and that approval never finished. It is the new device.
e2e_approval_waiting: After the person said it's theirs, until the new device answers.
e2e_approval_waits: In Settings → Devices, while a device this one approved hasn't finished setting up: why removing devices and changing the keys wait.
e2e_approval_yes: [short] Answers e2e_approval_ask: yes, the new device is the person's.
e2e_backup: [short] The label of the encrypted backup's row in Settings → Devices: the copy of the encrypted conversations kept in the account's storage.
e2e_backup_paused: Under e2e_backup in Settings → Devices, once the account's storage was too full to keep a day of the encrypted backup: it tries again each day.
e2e_backup_restoring: Under e2e_backup in Settings → Devices, and in a bar at the bottom of the app, while a new device brings in the encrypted backup: {done} is how many of its days came in, {total} how many there are, each a number already written out.
e2e_backup_too_large: Under e2e_backup in Settings → Devices, once a day of an encrypted conversation was too large for the storage to keep as one file: it tries again each day.
e2e_backup_up_to_date: [short] Under e2e_backup in Settings → Devices: nothing of the encrypted backup waits to go up.
e2e_backup_uploading: [short] Under e2e_backup in Settings → Devices: days of the encrypted conversations are going up to the account's storage, or wait to.
e2e_before_joining: A line at the start of a direct message or group the person joined after it began: the messages sent before they joined aren't on this device, and another member can share that history with them.
e2e_blocked: A line over the message box of a direct message or group whose encryption broke (a change no member's device could check came in): nothing more can be sent there until it restarts.
e2e_blocked_restart: [short] The button beside e2e_blocked, for the group's owner (in a direct message, either person): starts the conversation's encryption again (a verb).
e2e_blocked_wait: Follows e2e_blocked for the members who can't restart it. {owner} is the name of the group's owner, who can.
e2e_cancel: [short] The button that closes a dialog without doing what it asks: e2e_device_remove_title's, or an approval's question once the person said yes.
e2e_change_keys: [short] A button and a row of Settings → Devices: makes new security keys and a new recovery key for the account (a verb).
e2e_change_keys_line: Under e2e_change_keys in Settings → Devices: when to use it.
e2e_change_unanswered: Adding or removing a member got no answer from the server: the app sends it again by itself.
e2e_change_waits: In the add-members sheet or the remove dialog of an encrypted group, when an earlier change of its members still waits for the server's answer.
e2e_code_accept: [short] The button beside the code's field: checks the code typed (a verb).
e2e_code_accepted: On the new device once its code was accepted: the person confirms on the device that shows it.
e2e_code_fingerprint: 16 characters in four groups that identify what a new device asks for, which both devices show for the person to compare. {fingerprint} is those characters.
e2e_code_fingerprint_box_line: Under e2e_code_fingerprint on the new device, in the desktop app, which shows the same fingerprint in a box of its own, «Set up this device», outside the window.
e2e_code_fingerprint_line: Under e2e_code_fingerprint on the new device, on the web, which has no box of its own.
e2e_code_label: [short] The label of the field where the person types the six digits another device of theirs shows.
e2e_code_mismatch: Under the code's field, when the digits typed aren't those the approving device shows.
e2e_code_waiting: After e2e_use_code, until a device of the person's answers: what to do there.
e2e_cutover: A line at the start of a conversation from before end-to-end encryption came. {date} is the day those older messages were deleted, written out (24 November 2026).
e2e_delete_device: [short] A button in the bar about encrypted conversations, when this device's encrypted data can no longer be opened: deletes it, and sets the device up as a new one.
e2e_delete_device_confirm: Asks before e2e_delete_device does it, on a device that isn't on the person's device list.
e2e_delete_device_line: Under e2e_delete_device in Settings → Devices: what it does.
e2e_delete_listed_device_confirm: Asks before e2e_delete_device does it, on a device on the person's device list beside others: what's lost without the recovery key, unless another device still holds it, and that this device stays on that list until another of the person's devices removes it.
e2e_delete_only_device_confirm: Asks before e2e_delete_device does it, on the only device on the person's device list: what's lost without the recovery key.
e2e_delete_refused: A toast when the server refuses for good the deletion of the person's own encrypted message: it's gone on this device, but not for the others.
e2e_device_action_failed: In the dialog of e2e_device_remove_title when the removal didn't go through.
e2e_device_added: A notice the app shows once when a device is added to the person's account (someone signed in on it). {name} is that device's name (Duvet for Windows, Chrome on Linux, a phone's model).
e2e_device_by_id: In e2e_device_remove_away: a device Duvet no longer lists that this device knows nothing of, by the start of its ID ({id}).
e2e_device_id_start: In the dialog of e2e_device_remove_title: the first characters of the device's ID ({id}), as the app's own confirmation names the device by its whole ID.
e2e_device_known: In e2e_device_remove_away: a device Duvet no longer lists, by what this device knows of it: its name ({name}), what it runs ({client}, as its device list shows it) and when it was added ({date}).
e2e_device_lost: A checkbox in the dialog of e2e_device_remove_title, for a device the person no longer has: its removal makes new security keys too.
e2e_device_lost_note: Under the checkbox of e2e_device_lost: what new keys do, and what they bring (a new recovery key to save, and a notice the person's contacts see).
e2e_device_not_set_up: [short] A tag on a device's row in Settings → Devices: it's signed in, but wasn't set up to read encrypted conversations.
e2e_device_remove: [short] A button on a device's row in Settings → Devices: takes that device off the person's account (a verb).
e2e_device_remove_along: In the dialog of e2e_device_remove_title and the confirmation of e2e_change_keys: other devices ({names}, a list of their names) that an earlier removal took off but never finished, which this one takes off too.
e2e_device_remove_away: In the dialog of e2e_device_remove_title and the confirmation of e2e_change_keys, one for each: a device ({device}: e2e_device_known, or e2e_device_by_id) that Duvet no longer lists on the account, which the device list this removal signs takes off too; the person cancels if they removed nothing and changed no password, as a new password takes devices off.
e2e_device_remove_changed: Under the dialog of e2e_device_remove_title, or as the confirmation of e2e_change_keys fails: the devices the removal or change of keys would take off are others than the dialog named, so nothing was done; the dialog names them again.
e2e_device_remove_text: In the dialog of e2e_device_remove_title: what removing the device does to it.
e2e_device_remove_title: The title of the dialog that asks before a device is taken off the account. {name} is that device's name.
e2e_device_seen: Under a device's name in Settings → Devices. {client} is the app and version it signed in with, as Duvet writes it (desktop-windows/1.2.0, web/1.2.0); {date} is the day it last connected, written out.
e2e_device_unfinished: In Settings → Devices, when a removal fails because a device this one approved never finished setting up.
e2e_devices: [short] The Devices section of Settings, in its side panel and as its title: the places the person is signed in to Duvet with encrypted direct messages.
e2e_devices_failed: In Settings → Devices when the list of the person's devices couldn't be fetched; e2e_try_again follows it.
e2e_devices_lead: The line at the top of Settings → Devices. A device list is the account's signed list of the devices that may read encrypted conversations.
e2e_devices_loading: In Settings → Devices while the list of the person's devices is being fetched.
e2e_dismiss: [short] The label of the × that hides the bar about encrypted conversations until the page loads again (for a screen reader).
e2e_edit_refused: A toast when the server refuses for good an edit of the person's own encrypted message: this device shows it, the others don't.
e2e_failed: A bar at the bottom of the app: the database of encrypted conversations didn't open on this device, or the server refused this device. Duvet tries again by itself when it can.
e2e_file_altered: Shown on a file of an encrypted message whose bytes don't match what its message says of them.
e2e_file_download_failed: Shown on a file of an encrypted message that didn't come down or open now (no connection, the server, the app's engine not ready): a click tries again.
e2e_file_encrypted: Settings → Attachments: the name of a file of an encrypted conversation whose message this device doesn't hold, as only the message names it.
e2e_file_named: The label read out for an encrypted message's file card while it downloads or isn't shown; {name} is the file's name, {status} what the card says of it (its progress, or why it isn't shown).
e2e_file_play: The label read out for the button that downloads and plays a video of an encrypted message.
e2e_file_progress: [short] How far a file of an encrypted message is downloaded and decrypted; {percent} is a whole number from 0 to 100.
e2e_file_save: [short] A button (a verb) that saves a file of an encrypted message to the computer, as a download.
e2e_file_save_named: The label read out for the button that saves a file; {name} is the file's name.
e2e_file_show: The label read out for the button that downloads a picture of an encrypted message again, after it left the app's memory.
e2e_file_unavailable: Shown on a file of an encrypted message whose message doesn't name a file the server keeps, or whose size can't be its own.
e2e_files_gone: Shown on an encrypted message, as it waits and when the person retries it, whose files went with the app's last run: it can only be dismissed.
e2e_finish: [short] The button of e2e_first_device_finish: finishes setting up encryption (a verb).
e2e_finish_keys: [short] A row's label in Settings → Devices while a change of the person's security keys waits to be finished; e2e_finish is its button.
e2e_finish_without: [short] The button that finishes that change of security keys without the devices taken off the account; on the desktop the system's own box asks again first.
e2e_first_device: A bar at the bottom of the app, on the user's first device once direct messages are end-to-end encrypted: the button beside it (e2e_set_up) makes the user's keys and shows their recovery key.
e2e_first_device_finish: The same bar, when the app closed after making the keys and before saving them: the button beside it (e2e_finish) shows the recovery key again.
e2e_first_list_leaves_out: A bar at the bottom of the app on a device just set up, after a password change removed the person's devices. {devices} is a list of the start of their IDs.
e2e_gate: The name of the bar about encrypted conversations, for a screen reader.
e2e_gif_failed: Shown when a GIF picked in an encrypted conversation couldn't be downloaded to send as a file.
e2e_inactive_device: [short] A tag on a device's row in Settings → Devices: it hasn't connected to Duvet in 45 days. Said word for word in the mobile app too.
e2e_inactive_warning: A notice the app shows once for each device of the person's that hasn't connected in 45 days. {device} is that device's name (Duvet for Windows, Chrome on Linux, a phone's model).
e2e_key_changed: A notice over the message box of each conversation with someone whose security keys changed (a new device setup or new keys of theirs, or someone else's). {name} is their name.
e2e_key_changed_close: [short] The label of the × that closes a changed key's notice (a verb).
e2e_key_changed_verified: After e2e_key_changed, for someone the person had verified; also the question before their next message goes. {name} is the contact's name, or several joined as a list.
e2e_keys_again: In the encryption bar and in Settings → Devices, after a change of the security keys went on without devices that had left the account: one of them may still hold those keys, so another change is offered.
e2e_leave_elsewhere: In the Leave group dialog of an encrypted group, when this device isn't in the group's encryption (not joined yet, or waiting to be let back in): the person leaves from another of their devices.
e2e_leave_failed: In the Leave group dialog, when leaving failed for another reason.
e2e_loading_message: Read out for an encrypted message whose row this device hasn't read yet, which shows as a pulsing bar.
e2e_locked: A bar at the bottom of the desktop app: another Duvet window (another copy of the app, or another account's browser tab) has the encrypted conversations open.
e2e_lost_key: A bar at the bottom of the app: the key of this device's encrypted data is gone (cleared from the system's keyring or the browser), so it can't be read again. Beside it, e2e_delete_device.
e2e_mark_verified: [short] The button under a contact's security number: the person compared it with the contact's and marks them verified (a verb).
e2e_members_accept: [short] The button beside e2e_members_changed: the person accepts the members the conversation has now, and their device joins it with them.
e2e_members_blocked: In the add-members sheet or the remove dialog of an encrypted group, when this device can't change its members (the group's encryption is blocked, or this device isn't in it yet).
e2e_members_changed: A line over the message box of a conversation from before end-to-end encryption, whose members aren't the ones this device first saw there: it doesn't join until the person accepts them (e2e_members_accept).
e2e_members_now: Under "This conversation's members changed since you last saw it.": {names} is the conversation's members today, as a list.
e2e_new_device: A bar at the bottom of the app, on a device of a user who already has encrypted conversations on another device: this one needs their recovery key or another device's approval to read them.
e2e_new_device_finish: A bar at the bottom of the app: this device was set up, but the server doesn't list it yet (the app closed, or the person said no), and Finish does it.
e2e_no_approver: On the new device, when the person's account has no other device set up to approve it.
e2e_no_device: Over an encrypted conversation's message box: {name} is the members who have no device that can read it yet, as a list ("Bo and Cy").
e2e_no_e2e_here: In a direct message, on a platform where encrypted direct messages don't work yet (macOS and Linux): they work in the web app, at duvet.chat. Duvet is the app's name.
e2e_not_ready: Shown when this device's encryption isn't ready yet (still opening its conversations, or open in another window): under a message to an encrypted conversation that couldn't be sent, and in place of an encrypted conversation's search results.
e2e_paused: Shown when the person sends a message while the server has paused encrypted conversations: the message waits on this device and goes once they're back.
e2e_qr_label: What a screen reader says of the QR code under e2e_setup_qr_line.
e2e_range_all: [short] As e2e_range_day: all of the conversation's messages this device holds.
e2e_range_day: [short] One of the choices of how far back to share a direct message's or group's history with a member (in the Share history dialog), and how far back a member shared it: the last 24 hours. Starts with a lowercase letter, as it's also part of a sentence; the dialog capitalizes it.
e2e_recovery_continue: [short] The recovery key dialog's button, usable once e2e_recovery_saved is ticked: saves the user's keys and closes the dialog.
e2e_recovery_copied: [short] The Copy button's words for a moment after it copied the recovery key.
e2e_recovery_copy: [short] A button in the recovery key dialog: copies the key (a verb).
e2e_recovery_download: [short] A button in the recovery key dialog: saves the key as a text file (a verb).
e2e_recovery_failed: Under the recovery key dialog's button, when the keys couldn't be saved (usually no connection): the key stays the same, and pressing the button again tries again.
e2e_recovery_file: The first line of the text file the recovery key is downloaded in, above the key. Duvet is the app's name.
e2e_recovery_key: The label of the recovery key's field on a new device, and what a screen reader says of the recovery key's groups as the app shows them.
e2e_recovery_key_mistyped: Under the recovery key's field, when a character of what the person typed is off.
e2e_recovery_key_use: [short] The button under the recovery key's field: sets this device up with it (a verb).
e2e_recovery_key_wrong: Under the recovery key's field, when the key is one but not this account's current one.
e2e_recovery_later: [short] A button beside the recovery key dialog's error, once its upload failed: closes the dialog; the key is kept, and a Finish button in the bar shows it again to upload it.
e2e_recovery_saved: [short] The checkbox in the recovery key dialog that the user ticks once they saved the key: nothing goes on before it.
e2e_recovery_title: The title of the dialog that shows the user's recovery key once, which they need to read their encrypted conversations on a new device.
e2e_recovery_why: Under that title: why the recovery key matters. It's shown only now: the app doesn't keep it.
e2e_remove_failed: In the dialog that removes a member from a group, when the removal failed for another reason.
e2e_removed_device: A bar at the bottom of the app: another of the user's devices took this one off their account, so it no longer reads their encrypted conversations. Beside it, e2e_set_up_again.
e2e_reset_finish: A bar at the bottom of the app: the person started over, and the new keys wait to go up, which Finish does after their recovery key shows again.
e2e_restart_leaves_out: The question before restarting a blocked encrypted conversation's encryption: {names} is the people the restart leaves out, as a list.
e2e_restart_to_update: [short] A button under "Update Duvet" in a direct message, once the desktop app has downloaded its new version: restarts the app into it. The same words as the title bar's button.
e2e_restarting: [short] That button once pressed, while the app closes to open again on its new version.
e2e_rotation_finish: A bar the app shows when a change of the person's security keys stopped before it was saved; e2e_finish follows it, which finishes it.
e2e_rotation_gone: In the bar of a change of the person's security keys and in Settings → Devices: the change can't be saved with devices another of the person's devices took off the account meanwhile, which it can go on without. {devices}: those devices, each by the first eight characters of its ID (their names went with them), as a list.
e2e_rotation_relisted: In the bar of a change of the person's security keys and in Settings → Devices: another of the person's devices changed the keys first and kept a device this one's change takes off, so this device can't take those keys; deleting its data, and setting it up again, is the only way out.
e2e_rotation_stuck: In the bar of a change of the person's security keys and in Settings → Devices: the change can't be saved, as another of the person's devices changed the account's devices or keys meanwhile, so the recovery key it showed opens nothing; the ways out are a change of keys made on another of their devices, or deleting this device's data and setting it up again.
e2e_rotation_why: The text of the dialog that shows the new recovery key after the person changed their security keys (its title is e2e_recovery_title).
e2e_safety_changed: In the security number's dialog, when the contact's keys changed while it was open: the number shown now is their new one. {name} is the contact's name.
e2e_safety_compare: Under a contact's security number and its code: how to check it. {name} is the contact's name.
e2e_safety_digits: The screen reader's name of a contact's 60-digit security number, and the dialog's line under its title. {name} is the contact's name.
e2e_safety_failed: In the security number's dialog, when the number couldn't be loaded for a reason that passes.
e2e_safety_loading: In the security number's dialog while the number loads.
e2e_safety_none: In the security number's dialog, for a contact without encrypted conversations set up. {name} is the contact's name.
e2e_safety_qr_label: The screen reader's name of the code another phone scans to check the security number. {name} is the contact's name.
e2e_search_split: Shown in place of an encrypted conversation's search results, when the search mixes what only the server can look for (pinned:, has:sticker) with what only this device can (words, has:image, has:video, has:sound). pinned:, has:sticker, has:image, video and sound are the search's filters, typed as they are: keep them in English.
e2e_send_anyway: [short] The button of the question asked before a message goes, after a verified contact's keys changed: send it all the same (a verb).
e2e_server_key_changed: The encryption bar at the bottom of the app, on a device that's ready: the server signs its groups with another key than the one this device saw first and keeps, so encrypted conversations under the new key won't open on it. The same words as the mobile app's.
e2e_set_up: [short] The button of e2e_first_device: sets up encryption (a verb).
e2e_set_up_again: [short] The button of e2e_removed_device: deletes this device's encrypted data and sets it up again as a new device (a verb).
e2e_setup_again: In the setup card, when another device of the person's changed their device list first, and this one has to start its setup over.
e2e_setup_approve_begin: [short] In the setup card, when no approval is under way: begins one, which shows its QR code.
e2e_setup_approve_heading: A heading of e2e_setup_title: setting the device up by approving it from a device of the person's that already reads their encrypted conversations.
e2e_setup_failed: In the setup card, when a step failed for a reason that passes (the network, the server).
e2e_setup_key_heading: A heading of e2e_setup_title: setting the device up with the 48-character recovery key the person saved.
e2e_setup_qr_line: Beside the QR code a new device shows, which the person's phone scans to approve it.
e2e_setup_start_over_heading: A heading of e2e_setup_title: for a person with neither their recovery key nor another device.
e2e_setup_title: The title of the card that sets up a new device of the person's for their encrypted conversations.
e2e_share_history: [short] An item of a member's menu in an encrypted direct message or group: opens the dialog that shares the conversation's earlier messages with them (a verb).
e2e_share_history_failed: In the Share history dialog, when sharing failed for a reason the server didn't give.
e2e_share_history_limit: In the Share history dialog: the person shared history 10 times in the last hour, the most allowed. {when} is when they can try again, a relative time such as 'in 12 minutes'.
e2e_share_history_line: Under the Share history dialog's title: what the member gets. {name} is the member; the messages show to them marked as shared by the person.
e2e_share_history_no_device: In the Share history dialog: the member has no device set up for encrypted conversations, so nothing can be shared with them yet. {name} is the member.
e2e_share_history_send: [short] The Share history dialog's button that shares (a verb).
e2e_share_history_sharing: [short] The Share history dialog's button while the history goes up.
e2e_share_history_truncated: In the Share history dialog once it shared: the history was too big for one package, so only the newest messages went. {name} is the member, {date} the day from which they get every message.
e2e_share_history_with: The title of the Share history dialog. {name} is the member the history goes to.
e2e_shared: A line in a direct message or group, where its members see that one of them shared the conversation's earlier messages with another: {a} shared them, {b} got them, {range} how far back (day, week, month, or anything else for all of them).
e2e_shared_add: [short] The button beside e2e_shared_with_you: adds the messages another member shared to this device's copy of the conversation (a verb).
e2e_shared_add_failed: Beside e2e_shared_with_you, when adding the shared messages to this device failed.
e2e_shared_by: [short] Under a message in a direct message or group that another member shared with this device (a shared history). {name} is who shared it.
e2e_shared_with_you: As e2e_shared, for the person who got them: {a} shared them with the person reading; also the offer over the message box to add them.
e2e_start_over: [short] The button under e2e_start_over_line, and the button that confirms e2e_start_over_warning (a verb).
e2e_start_over_confirm: A confirmation before the device's encrypted data is deleted and the device set up again as a new one (Set up again, or Remove this device and delete its data). The other devices of the user keep their data.
e2e_start_over_line: Under e2e_setup_start_over_heading: what starting over does.
e2e_start_over_warning: Asks before starting over: what the person loses, and what their contacts see.
e2e_storage_not_kept: In Settings → Devices, on the web only: the browser didn't promise to keep the site's data, so it may delete it, and the person's encrypted conversations with it.
e2e_this_device: [short] A tag on the row of the device the person is using now, in Settings → Devices.
e2e_too_long: [short] Shown when an encrypted message is past the size the server takes (32 KiB once encrypted).
e2e_too_many_waiting: Shown when a new message to an encrypted conversation is refused because too many of the person's messages there still wait to be sent.
e2e_try_again: [short] A button that fetches the list of devices again (a verb).
e2e_unsupported_browser: A bar at the bottom of the web app, in a browser that lacks what encrypted conversations need.
e2e_update: Shown in a direct message when this version of the app is too old for encrypted direct messages (a verb: update the app). Under it, the download page's address or a Restart to update button. Duvet is the app's name.
e2e_use_code: [short] A button under the QR code: approve the device by a six-digit code instead of the QR (a phrase).
e2e_verified: [short] The mark beside a contact's name once the person verified their security number, and the words beside it in the dialog (an adjective).
e2e_verify_number: [short] In a contact's profile and menu, and on a changed key's notice: opens their security number to compare and verify (a verb); also the dialog's title.
e2e_wait_owner: A line over the message box of a new group whose encryption its owner hasn't set up yet: nobody can send until they open it. {owner} is the owner's name.
e2e_wait_rejoin: A line over the message box of a conversation this device can't read yet (it was set up again): another member's device lets it back in as soon as it opens the conversation.
e2e_waiting: [short] In place of a message's text in a direct message or group, when this device couldn't open its copy yet.
e2e_waiting_detail: Follows e2e_waiting: the message shows once the device it was sent from passes it on.
format_size_bytes: [short] A file's size under a kilobyte. {size} is the number, written in the language's digits.
format_size_kb: [short] A file's size in kilobytes, e.g. 12.5 KB. Use your language's unit (French: Ko).
format_size_mb: [short] A file's size in megabytes, e.g. 3.25 MB. Use your language's unit (French: Mo).
public_app_connecting: Beside a spinner while the app connects, before anything else shows.
public_app_open_chat_failed: A notice when a direct message with someone couldn't be opened or started.
public_app_resize_sidebar: Screen reader name of the sidebar's right edge, which is dragged (or moved with the arrow keys) to make the sidebar wider or narrower.
public_download_other_systems: Under the download button. duvet.chat is the website's address: keep it as it is.
public_download_page_title: The browser tab's title of the download page. Duvet is the app's name.
public_download_title: Heading of the download page (a verb: get the app). Duvet is the app's name.
public_download_windows: [short] The download page's button: the installer for Windows.
public_invite_bad_link: The invite link opened is broken: it has no invite code, or a wrong one.
public_invite_go_back: [short] A button on an invite that can't be used: goes back to the start page.
public_invite_invited: <line>…</line> is the small line over the Space's name; <name>{space}</name> is the name, drawn as the card's heading. Keep both tags; either may come first. Put every word inside one of them: words outside the tags show unstyled between the line and the heading.
public_invite_join: [short] The invite card's button: join the Space (a verb).
public_invite_join_failed: Shown on the invite card when joining the Space failed.
public_invite_joining: [short] The invite card's button while the Space is being joined.
public_invite_loading: Beside a spinner while the invite is looked up.
public_invite_members: On the invite card: how many members the Space has, capitalised as a label. # is the number.
public_invite_not_now: [short] The invite card's last button: leave without joining.
public_invite_sign_in: [short] The invite card's button when signed out: sign in, then join the Space.
public_invite_sign_in_note: On the invite card when signed out, over the button "Sign in to join".
public_invite_unavailable: Heading when an invite link can't be used: it's wrong, expired or used up.
public_settings_window_title: The title of the Settings window. Duvet is the app's name.
public_space_settings_window_title: The title of a Space's settings window, before the Space's name is known.
public_space_settings_window_title_named: The title of a Space's settings window. {space} is the Space's name, as its people wrote it.
settings_cancel: [short] The button that closes the sign-out dialog without signing out.
settings_language_note: Under the language picker in Settings › Appearance. Messages are what people send each other: the app never translates them.
settings_language_system: [short] The picker's first choice: follow the computer's language. {language} is that language's name in itself, e.g. Español.
settings_sign_out: [short] The button that signs the person out of Duvet, in Settings and in its dialog (a verb).
settings_sign_out_text: In the sign-out dialog: signing out keeps this device's encrypted conversations; deleting them is a button of its own there (e2e_delete_device).
settings_sign_out_title: The title of the dialog that asks before the person signs out.
